why: The sieve of Eratosthenes: instead of testing each number, cross out the multiples of every prime p starting at p*p; whatever stays uncrossed is prime, in O(n log log n).
hints: Testing each number by trial division is about O(n sqrt n). Can you mark composites instead?
Every composite has a prime factor <= its square root. For each prime p with p*p < n, mark p*p, p*p+p, ... as composite.
Boolean array of size n, 0 and 1 not prime, loop p while p*p < n, then collect the unmarked indices. O(n log log n) time, O(n) memory.
pitfalls: Primes strictly less than n: n itself is excluded, and n = 0, 1, 2 return [].
Start crossing out at p*p, not 2p (smaller multiples were crossed by smaller primes).
n is up to 5*10^6: use a compact boolean array (bytearray in Python).
